items.title: How to tell if an Android app is spying on your phone, and the best ways to catch it
items.summary:

items.title: GameNative just fixed PC gaming on Pixels and Exynos-powered Galaxy phones
items.summary:
Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

The GameNative v1.4.1 release preview is now available and brings much better support for non-Snapdragon devices. 
 The update specifically fixes major graphical problems on devices like the Pixel 6 to Pixel 10, as well as Exynos-powered Galaxy phones. 
 This GameNative release also brings an Optimize feature that tunes your game based on preset goals. 

GameNative is still one of the best ways to locally run PC games on your Android device. The app works best on Snapdragon-powered devices, although the team previously introduced support for other chipmakers a while back. Now, the latest update brings great news if you’ve got a Pixel or Exynos-powered device.

GameNative v1.4.1 has been released on GitHub as a preview, and it brings updated support for devices with Mali, PowerVR, and Xclipse graphics. The team specifically updated the “wrapper-gamenative” graphics driver. Check out the table below for a better idea of what’s been fixed.
items.t: GameNative just fixed PC gaming on Pixels and Exynos-powered Galaxy phones

items.title: Motorola Razr Flex 2027 leaks point to a new Snapdragon chip, Android 17, and a wide design
items.summary:
TL;DR 

A certification document lists an unreleased Snapdragon SM8845 Pro chipset and Android 17 for what’s believed to be the Motorola Razr Flex 2027. 
 The document also points to an under-display fingerprint scanner, Bluetooth 6.0, and face unlock. 
 A purported image of the phone shows a compact, wide foldable design consistent with previously leaked concept renders. 

Motorola spent years making foldable phones that could shrink to fit your pocket before finally going big with the Razr Fold . But having explored both ends of the foldable spectrum, the company’s next move could land somewhere in between. Earlier this month, we spotted the Motorola Razr Flex 2027 on the company’s own website, lending credibility to earlier leaks suggesting that Motorola was working on a different kind of foldable. Now, newly surfaced certification documents and an alleged image of the phone give us a clearer idea of what Motorola might have in mind, inside and out.

A security certification document identifies a Motorola device codenamed Parker (XT2761) running Android 17. That model number has already been linked to the Razr Flex 27 through regulatory filings in the UAE , but what’s particularly interesting is the processor listed inside: Qualcomm’s Snapdragon SM8845 Pro.
items.t: Motorola Razr Flex 2027 leaks point to a new Snapdragon chip, Android 17, and a wide design

Samsung appears to be working on a new camera feature called “Dual cam panorama.” 
 It will use the front and rear cameras to capture up to 360 degrees of your surroundings. 
 The feature isn’t live yet, but could make an appearance in future One UI 9.5 betas. 

The One UI 9.5 beta is finally here, and we’ve been taking a close look under the hood to spot upcoming features that aren’t yet enabled. We’ve already found evidence of a native Open Gate recording function , and it seems Samsung is prepping yet another new feature for the Camera app.

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

We found strings in the One UI 9.5 Camera app code that hint at a new feature called “Dual cam panorama.” The existing Panorama mode captures a wide scene by letting users move their phone in one direction. Dual cam panorama could let users capture a complete 360-degree view of their surroundings by using both the rear and front cameras in tandem.

items.title: One UI 9.5 could bring native full-sensor video recording to Galaxy phones
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Samsung is working on a native Open Gate recording option for the Camera app in One UI 9.5. 
 It will let users record video using the entire imaging area of the sensor for more cropping and stabilization options in post-production. 
 The feature will support several frame rates from 24fps to 60fps. 

Samsung has started rolling out the One UI 9.5 beta for the Galaxy S26 series , and it comes with several new features. However, Samsung is also working on plenty of features that aren’t yet enabled in the beta. This includes a new Camera app feature video enthusiasts will love: native Open Gate recording.

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

While digging into the new Camera app in One UI 9.5 , we found several strings suggesting that the company is preparing a new option for Open Gate video recording. Open Gate uses the entire imaging area of a camera sensor instead of cropping the footage to a standard widescreen format like 16:9. Since most camera sensors have a 4:3 aspect ratio, Open Gate captures a taller frame, giving users more options for cropping and stabilization in post-production.
items.t: One UI 9.5 could bring native full-sensor video recording to Galaxy phones

Motorola has put up a teaser page on Flipkart for the Motorola Edge 70 Neo in India. The company will officially launch the phone on November 24 - next Tuesday.

The images on the page show the phone in a sage-like hue, with a raised rounded-square camera island on the back and a curved display with a centered punch-hole up front. The camera ring reads "50MP", "Ultra HDR", "OIS", and "Lytia". Motorola is also highlighting AI photo editing done just by asking, with "add butterfly on shoulder" as the example prompt.

items.title: YouTube ‘Co-Views’ try to guess how many people are watching your TV, rolling out now
items.summary:
Following a change in how it counts views earlier this year, YouTube is now announcing “Co-Views” as a way for the platform to try and guess how many people are watching a YouTube video on a TV, and it counts towards the video’s total view count.

items.title: The Sideload 052: Pebble’s back. Now what?
items.summary:
Welcome to episode 52 of The Sideload, a 9to5Google podcast. This week, Will and Daniel are joined by Eric Migicovsky, who sold Pebble to Fitbit back in 2016 only to bring its watches back from the grave a decade later. Together, the crews get into everything from the story behind Pebble’s open-sourcing, how Eric’s needs have shaped the core experience, and why he has no interest in an OLED Pebble watch.
